ai.description: Duttaphrynus mamitensis is a small toad reaching 35–45 mm. It is brown with dark dorsal mottling and a pale mid-dorsal stripe. Key features include prominent parotoid glands and granular skin.
ai.identificationRemarks: Duttaphrynus mamitensis is best distinguished by its distinct, elongated parotoid glands that are significantly longer than the diameter of the eye.
ai.habitat: Duttaphrynus mamitensis inhabits subtropical evergreen forests in Mizoram, India, typically found at elevations between 700 and 900 meters near streams and rocky areas.
ai.behavior: Mamit’s toad is primarily nocturnal, emerging after dark to forage for small invertebrates among the leaf litter of its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: Duttaphrynus mamitensis breeds during the monsoon season (June–August), depositing eggs in long, gelatinous strings within shallow, stagnant water bodies.
ai.distributionRemarks: Duttaphrynus mamitensis is endemic to Mizoram in Northeast India, where it is found at elevations between 700 and 900 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Duttaphrynus mamitensis* consists of a series of short, pulsed notes with a low pitch, typically heard from vegetation near forest streams.
